lead_headline: Restaurant data erupts: 3 fresh leads detected today after quiet weekend — Sandomi at Edgewater Public Market, Marczyk FineBurger at Northfield, Caveman Chefs closure

restaurant.blurb: 3 leads today: Sandomi (Japanese sandos/banh mi) opened at Edgewater Public Market, Marczyk FineBurger debuted at Northfield, Caveman Chefs meal delivery closed.

liquor.blurb: The application freeze hits 39 days. Zero new filings today extends the unprecedented licensing silence that began June 1. The database tracks 12,325 active licenses but hasn't logged a single new bar, restaurant, or retail application since early June — now the longest drought in modern tracking history. Post-holiday Mondays historically restart the pipeline with 2-3 applications. Not this time. Whether capital scarcity, state backlogs, or fundamental shifts in hospitality investment are driving the void remains unclear. The first filing will mark the end of an anomaly that's rewriting baseline expectations for Colorado's liquor licensing velocity.

reputation.blurb: 3 mentions yesterday — the post-holiday recovery begins. Week closes at 59 mentions across 18 sources, down 18% from last week's 72. Facebook leads with 19 citations, Reddit contributes 16, X.com adds 4, Hoodline and Instagram each log 3. Google News RSS captured 58 of 59 discoveries. Top stories: Downtown developer's $10.6M power play next to Upton Towers, Pueblo Crossing development plans submitted, Denver Club closure struggles. The holiday week typically compresses volume — last Monday's 0-mention holiday nadir now reversing. Tuesday's numbers will clarify whether the 18% weekly decline signals summer slowdown or just holiday compression before a return to June's 60-70 citation baseline.

subscriptions.blurb: Net flat yesterday (0 new, 0 canceled) — the fourth consecutive zero-net day. MTD stays at +9 (+1.5/day), 90-day net holds at +117. July opened with promise: the June 29-30 surge (+17 in 48 hours) carried momentum through July 1-3 (+10 net over three days). Then the freeze: four straight days of zero movement (July 4-7). The +1.5/day MTD pace still beats YTD baseline (+1.3/day), but barely. Remove the June 29-30 spike and July flattens to near-zero. The 7-day window (+22 net) masks the stall — it's propped up entirely by the explosive June close. Holiday timing muddies the read, but the pattern echoes June's pre-surge doldrums when a −9 week preceded the breakout. Tuesday's numbers will determine if this is holiday noise or a genuine reversal of June's closing momentum.
